requirement:
The requirements index MUST link to its execution-coverage subchapter under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index`.
rationale:
**Obligation.** `requirements.test-coverage.index.navigation` has one obligation. The requirements index chapter MUST link to its generated execution-coverage subchapter. The cited `requirements.test-coverage.index` governs generation, and that behavior is not reassessed here.

**Implementation.** `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#fn[populate_in]` is the only {impl} site. It finds the chapter whose path equals `parent`. It appends a `[Coverage gaps](<relative href>)` link to that chapter's content. It then inserts the generated coverage chapter as the first sub-item. The link is added in one place, with no separate branch for different kinds of parent.

**Test.** `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_reports_inherit_the_requirements_index_hierarchy]` carries the {test} reference. It builds a parent chapter at `reports.md` and calls `populate_in` on it. It then asserts `parent.content.contains("[Coverage gaps](reports/coverage.html)")`. That assertion checks the link text and the correct relative target, so a missing or wrong link would fail it. The test runs for a numbered parent and an unnumbered parent, which covers the two situations in which the parent chapter might differ. It also asserts that the coverage chapter is the parent's first sub-item with the expected path. The link therefore points at a chapter that exists.

**Gaps.** I found none. The requirement states no further cases, such as a failure mode or a MAY or SHOULD clause. The explicit versus automatic placement of the index belongs to `requirements.test-coverage.index`. `populate_in` receives the resolved parent path either way, so the link behavior is the same in both cases.
